subject: Next steps: dev sandbox & local validation plan (Python/TS samples + auth/routing)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Hart <amelia@triviumhealth.com>, Luis Ramirez <luis.ramirez@triviumhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: dev sandbox & local validation plan (Python/TS samples + auth/routing)

Hi Amelia / Luis —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so your engineering team can spin up a local proof-of-concept with minimal effort: 

Key goals we agreed on:
- Validate auth and routing for private data (SSO-backed API + per-route policy)
- Test structured output / tool-calling with one sandbox tool (calendar lookup)
- Run embeddings + reranker pipeline on a small dataset (10–20 documents)
- Confirm latency/cost profile on a representative dev workload

What I’m sharing here: a lightweight sandbox checklist and a tiny sample repo that contains both Python and TypeScript starter apps (local server + example calls). Attachments: redwood-sandbox-checklist.pdf and sample-repo-links.txt. Repo includes a Docker Compose file so you can run everything locally and a script to populate a small embedding index. 

Simple local flow (recommended):
1) Clone the sample repo and set environment variables (REDFWD_API_KEY_SANDBOX, REDFWD_SSO_CLIENT, REDFWD_ROUTER_ID)
2) Run `docker-compose up` (containers: local proxy, sample app, mock tool)
3) In the Python app: `python examples/local_run.py --mode=structured` — this will exercise tool calling and structured output parsing
4) In the TS app: `pnpm install && pnpm start` then call `/test/embed` to ingest sample docs and run a basic rerank request

Auth notes:
- We’ll provision a sandbox API key scoped to the trial dataset and a short-lived OAuth client for your engineers to try the SSO flow.
- For routing tests we recommend two routes: `fast` (gpt-4-like runtime) and `economy` (quantized ACU) so you can compare latency/cost.

Open asks for Trivium team (can you confirm by EOD Monday?):
- A contact for your infra lead to receive the sandbox API key (email + phone)
- Confirm preferred SSO/IdP (Okta, Azure AD, or SAML details) for OAuth client provisioning
- A small docs sample (CSV or JSON, ~10 docs) we can seed into the embeddings index or we’ll provide a dummy set if you prefer

Proposed next interactions:
- Monday: we provision credentials and drop a step-by-step README into your team’s Slack channel (or shared Drive)
- Wednesday: 30-min pairing session to walk through the local run and validate routing/auth

Marissa / Karthik — tagging you both for the sample repo ownership and to confirm the Docker Compose ports (we recommend 8082 for the local proxy + 9090 for mock tool).

Amelia / Luis — happy to adjust depending on your windows. If you want us to send a pre-populated VM instead of docker-compose we can do that too (adds ~1 day).

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks Vanessa — this looks great and actionable. A few quick clarifications: 

- Our infra lead for the sandbox is Luis (cc’d). He prefers Okta; I’ll send an exported metadata file by EOD Monday.
- For the small docs sample, we’ll send a sanitized CSV with 12 records (PHI removed) — should be fine for embeddings.
- We’d prefer the Docker Compose route for initial validation. If it proves flaky we’ll request the VM.

Can you confirm the exact scope for the sandbox API key? We need to present it to security — mainly around data retention and logs.

Also — can Marissa share a one-page matrix mapping the two routing profiles (fast vs economy) to expected latency and cost-per-1k-tokens? That will help our procurement team.

Subject: Re: Next steps: dev sandbox & local validation plan (Python/TS samples + auth/routing)

Amelia — sending the routing/cost matrix inline (PDF attached in my reply to the drive link):

Routing profile summary (short):
- fast: target p50 < 80ms for 256-token responses; pre-warmed small GPU pool; estimated cost ~ $3.20 / 1k tokens (dev pricing)
- economy: p50 180–300ms for same prompt size; quantized model variant on mixed CPU/GPU; estimated cost ~ $0.45 / 1k tokens

Sandbox key scope: 
- Scoped to the `trivium-dev` project only
- No telemetry retention beyond 30 days by default; can be configured to 7/30/90 days (we’ll document)
- Logs: access logs retained for 30 days, audit logs for 90 days (we can provide SOC2 artifacts on request)

Karthik — I built the small Docker compose and test scripts. Ports are as Vanessa suggested. I’ll drop a short README to the repo and push a small perf script (`perf/latency_probe.sh`) that runs a 50-request burst to both routes and reports p50/p95.

Vanessa — I’ll attach the one-pager and the repo link to the HubSpot deal after you provision the key.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
